name: XTTS-v2
size: ~2 GB weights, ~4 GB RAM on Apple silicon (MPS)
note: Natural Turkish and clones a voice from a ~10 s clip. The company behind it shut down, so expect no updates; the licence rules out commercial use.

name: Piper (dfki Turkish)
languages: 30+ languages; Turkish has one voice (dfki, medium)
license: Piper: MIT (original, archived) / GPL-3.0 (maintained fork); the dfki voice data is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
size: ~60 MB voice, runs on CPU far faster than real time
note: Tiny and instant, but robotic. A fallback and a quick-reply voice rather than a nice one.

name: Kokoro
languages: English (US, UK), Spanish, French, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese, Chinese
size: 82M parameters, ~330 MB, runs on CPU in real time
note: The quick, light English voice. About fifty fixed voices; no cloning and no Turkish.

name: Chatterbox (Turbo and Multilingual)
languages: Multilingual V3: 23+ languages incl. Turkish; Turbo: English
size: ~0.5B parameters; needs a GPU or Apple silicon to feel quick
note: The English Turbo model is installed here. The Multilingual model (with Turkish and cross-language voice cloning) is a separate download that isn't installed.

name: VoxCPM2
size: 2B parameters, ~9.5 GB download; the card lists CUDA 12 as the requirement
note: 48 kHz, clones from a short clip and can design a voice from a text description. Heavy: the model card targets an NVIDIA GPU, so on this Mac it would be slow.

name: Ahenk (Turkish)
license: Code Apache-2.0; weights CC BY 4.0 (large model is a VoxCPM2 LoRA)
size: Ahenk Cep: 8.6M parameters, 34 MB, CPU at about 0.2x real time; Ahenk: 2B on GPU
note: Turkish-first, one designed synthetic voice with question intonation and emotions. The small Cep model runs in a browser tab, so it is the one worth trying on this server.

name: FreyaTTS-small
size: 183M parameters, ~730 MB; the card reports about 0.7x real time on a laptop CPU
note: A single Turkish speaker, no cloning. The card ranks it ahead of XTTS-v2 on its own Turkish error rate, which is the authors' own benchmark.

name: F5-TTS
languages: English and Chinese (other languages via community finetunes)
license: Code MIT; pre-trained models CC BY-NC 4.0
size: ~1.3 GB model; a GPU is advised
note: Good cloning in English. No official Turkish model and the weights are non-commercial; the Freya card measures it well behind on Turkish.

name: Seed-VC
languages: language-independent (changes who is speaking, not the words)
size: a few hundred MB; GPU advised for real time
note: Not a TTS: it turns one voice recording into another voice, with no training or a short reference. It would make a Turkish voice out of any TTS output.

name: RVC (Retrieval-based Voice Conversion)
size: small per-voice models; a GPU is advised
note: Voice conversion, not TTS: you train a model per target voice from a few minutes of audio. Mind consent when the target is a real person.
